reason: The arithmetic holds. I recomputed it with the existing scorer reimplementation on the same tail (reproduces the official exp39 TP/FP/FN). Global J goes from 122151/135729 = 0.90000 to 122221/(122221+6656+6662) = 0.90174. The D-weighted adjusted J goes from 0.90244 to 0.90422 (+0.00178, video-bootstrap CI90 [+0.0009, +0.0027]). dFN = -dTP, the node count is unchanged, so the node multiplier is unchanged, and the division counts are identical. The whole delta therefore lands 1:1 in the final score. The '0.9 x' factor in the proposal is wrong, because the edge term is not scaled. The mechanism is quantitatively consistent: z rounding adds RMS 1.625/sqrt(12) = 0.47 um, against about 900 theft near-ties with a margin under 2 um. Converting 70 FN plus 120 FP (via unevaluable edges) = +0.0018 fits. Transfer check: I added 1 um/axis Gaussian noise to mimic worse localisation on unseen embryos. The gain did not shrink: +0.0023 (0.87978 -> 0.88208). So the 60-90% transfer discount is, if anything, pessimistic. Weak points: 44b6 alone has a CI90 that crosses 0 ([-0.0005, +0.0043]). The idea is worth only about 8% of the 0.022 gap to the 0.97 target. The real downside is server-side truncation, measured at -0.004 overall and -0.0047 on 6bba. That risk may not show on the public embryo: truncation is +0.0002 on 44b6, so a 44b6-like public embryo would hide a private loss. The proposal's 'probe tells us what the server does' logic is therefore not reliable. This is repairable, see fix.
fix_if_any: Use a TRUNCATION-SAFE encoding instead of plain floats: w = round(v) + clip(v - round(v), 0, 0.499), written with 3 decimals, so floor(w) == round(w) == round(v). The server then scores exactly like today whether it rounds or int-truncates, and gets the float gain if it keeps Float64. Measured on 199 videos (scratchpad roundsafe.py): +0.00190 overall, CI90 [+0.00115, +0.00271] (plain float +0.00178). 6bba: +0.00195, CI90 [+0.00115, +0.00282]. 44b6: +0.00163, CI90 [-0.0009, +0.0038]. The only remaining failure mode is a parse error, which shows up as a failed submission. Keep every node coordinate formatted with a decimal point so polars infers Float64. Treat it as a bundle item, because it is at most ~0.002 of the 0.022 gap. For the lab gate, use the D-weighted delta with per-embryo CI and the win rate among changed videos only, since about 40-50% of videos tie exactly.
realistic_public_gain: +0.001 to +0.002 on public if the server keeps floats; the noise-proxy test suggests transfer near 100%. 0 if the server rounds or truncates, with the safe encoding. With plain floats plus truncation, public could look flat (44b6-like) while private loses about 0.004. The linefit retune on floats is unmeasured, maybe +0.0005 (guess). Roughly 8% of the gap to 0.97.
